title: API key is hard-coded in client JavaScript, contradicting the README's 'never leaves the server'
evidence: api.js is loaded by index.html:25 as a plain script; the key is sent in the Authorization header of both fetches (api.js:6, api.js:11). Driven in Chromium: GET /v1/orders went out from the browser carrying the header.
failing_case: Any visitor opens view-source or DevTools Network, copies the Bearer token and calls /refunds directly with it.
remediation: Remove the key from the bundle. Put the API behind a same-origin server route that holds the key and enforces who may list or refund. Rotate the key, since it has shipped.

title: Customer name (and order id) written into innerHTML unescaped
evidence: app.js:32 builds the row with a template string and tb.innerHTML +=. Driven: an order whose customer.name is `` on the visible page ran the handler (window.__x === 1). o.id in data-id="${o.id}" is an attribute sink with the same problem.
failing_case: A customer signs up with the name ``. When the operator views the orders page, the script runs in the page that holds the refund control and the API key (api.js:3), so it can read the key or POST refunds.
remediation: Build rows with createElement and textContent / setAttribute (or one escape function used at every sink); never interpolate data into innerHTML.

title: Selection list only ever grows: unchecking does not remove an id, and it is never cleared, so Refund selected refunds orders the user deselected
evidence: app.js:35 pushes on check and does nothing on uncheck; duplicates are pushed on re-check; renderTable rebuilds rows unchecked (app.js:30) while `selected` keeps the old ids; app.js:49-52 never clears it. Driven: check then uncheck row 11 -> selected = ['11']; after paging away and back, 0 boxes were checked but selected was unchanged.
failing_case: Check order 11, uncheck it, check order 12, click Refund selected. The request body contains ids [11,12]; order 11 is refunded though it shows unchecked. Ids also survive paging, searching, and a completed refund (a second click refunds the same orders again).
remediation: Keep selection as a Set keyed by id, updated on both check and uncheck; re-apply checked state when rendering; clear it after a confirmed refund; show the count next to the button.

title: The Refund control is a span: not focusable, no role, not operable by keyboard or screen reader
evidence: Driven: tabIndex = -1 and no role attribute. The click handler is bound in app.js:49 only to mouse click. Failure of WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard (A) and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A).
failing_case: A keyboard-only or screen-reader user checks orders but can never reach 'Refund selected' with Tab, so the main task cannot be done.
remediation: Use <button type="button" id="refundBtn">Refund selected</button> and style it; add a disabled state when nothing is selected.

quote: - **Secure:** the API key never leaves the server.
title: README says the API key never leaves the server; it is in api.js and sent from the browser
evidence: api.js:3 holds the key; api.js:6 and api.js:11 send it from client code. index.html:25 serves api.js.
failing_case: A reader or buyer relies on the README, ships this as is, and exposes the key to every visitor.
remediation: Fix the code (proxy the API from a server) and then state it, or remove the claim. Do not claim it while api.js:3 exists.

quote: - **Fully accessible:** meets WCAG 2.1 AA, including 44 px touch targets (criterion 2.5.5).
title: README claims full WCAG 2.1 AA and 44 px targets; the page fails both, and 2.5.5 is a AAA criterion in 2.1
evidence: Driven: Prev button measured 32.7 x 18 px. styles.css:18 sets 12px buttons with 2px 4px padding. Failures listed above: 2.1.1, 2.4.7, 1.4.1, 1.3.1, 1.4.3, 4.1.3. 2.5.5 is AAA in WCAG 2.1.
failing_case: A buyer or procurement reviewer relies on 'Fully accessible, WCAG 2.1 AA' and gets a page a keyboard user cannot use to refund.
remediation: Remove the claim until an audit passes; state the real conformance level and cite 2.5.5 as AAA (2.5.8 24 px is AA in 2.2).

quote: 12 seats on annual billing at 20% off is $1,440 a year.
title: Pricing arithmetic is wrong: 12 seats at $15 with 20% off is $1,728 a year, not $1,440
evidence: Per seat per month: 12 x 15 = 180 a month; x12 = 2,160 a year; 20% off = 1,728. Per seat per year: 12 x 15 = 180, less 20% = 144. $1,440 matches neither reading (it is 3,60 off 2,160 at a 33% discount).
failing_case: A customer quoted $1,440 a year is under-charged by $288 per account under the monthly reading, or a buyer who reads $15 as monthly is shown a 33% discount instead of 20%.
remediation: State the unit (per seat per month), and correct the figure to $1,728 a year. Compute it from the plan constants in one place that the docs and billing share.

quote: - Refunds are confirmed before they are sent.
title: README says refunds are confirmed before sending; the code sends on a single click with no confirmation
evidence: app.js:49-52: onclick calls refund(selected) immediately; no confirm(), dialog or undo anywhere in the payload. Driven: one click produced the POST.
failing_case: User mis-clicks the refund control (a span with no spacing from the filters) and money is refunded with no prompt, contrary to the stated behaviour.
remediation: Add a confirm step naming the count and total ('Refund 3 orders totalling $X?') with Cancel as default, or correct the README.

title: getOrders never checks the HTTP status, and load() has no catch: an error body crashes the page silently
evidence: api.js:7 parses whatever comes back; app.js:41 assigns it to `orders`. Driven with a JSON error object as the response: pageerror 'orders is not iterable' and the old table stays on screen with no message. A rejected fetch or non-JSON 502 body is an unhandled rejection.
failing_case: The API returns 401 (expired key) or 500. The table keeps stale data, stats are not updated, nothing tells the operator, and the console shows an exception.
remediation: Check res.ok, throw with the status, catch in load() and render an error state with a Retry button; validate that the payload is an array.

title: refund() never awaits the request and always returns ok:true, so the UI reports a refund that may have failed
evidence: api.js:11 calls fetch without await, without a status check and without a catch; api.js:12 returns ok:true immediately. Driven with the refunds endpoint answering HTTP 500: the toast still showed 'Refunded 2 orders!' and the POST was sent.
failing_case: Select two orders, click Refund selected while the API returns 500 (or the network is down). The toast says 'Refunded 2 orders!'. No money moved; the operator believes it did. A network failure also raises an unhandled promise rejection.
remediation: Make refund() async: await fetch, check res.ok, throw or return {ok:false, error} on failure; show the failure and a retry in the UI, and show success only after a 2xx.

title: Pagination starts at offset 10 on page 1, so the first 10 orders are never shown
evidence: page is initialised to 1 (app.js:3) and start = page * PAGE_SIZE. Driven with 25 orders: the first visible row was order 11; orders 1-10 appear on no page (page 0 is only reachable by pressing Prev, which shows 'Page 0').
failing_case: Open the dashboard with 25 orders: the table shows orders 11-20. Orders 1-10 cannot be found or refunded unless the operator searches for them.
remediation: Use (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE, or make page zero-based and display page + 1; add a test with 25 orders that checks every order is on exactly one page.

title: Page count rounds down and Prev/Next are unbounded, so the pager shows 'Page 3 of 2', 'Page -1 of 2' and blank tables; page is not reset when a search changes the results
evidence: app.js:34 uses floor, not ceil; app.js:47-48 decrement and increment with no limits; load() (app.js:38-43) never resets page. Driven with 25 orders: Next x3 -> 'Page 4 of 2' with 0 rows; Prev x5 -> 'Page -1 of 2'. 0 orders -> 'Page 1 of 0'.
failing_case: 25 orders: label reads 'Page 1 of 2' though 3 pages exist; clicking Next twice shows 'Page 3 of 2' and an empty table. Go to page 2, type a search with 5 results: the table is empty because page is still 2.
remediation: totalPages = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(n / PAGE_SIZE)); clamp page after every load and on Prev/Next; disable Prev/Next at the limits.

title: Every keystroke fires an unthrottled fetch, and whichever response arrives last overwrites the table
evidence: app.js:45 binds load to oninput directly; app.js:41 assigns `orders` after await with no check that the query is still current; no AbortController; no debounce.
failing_case: Type 'ab'. The request for q=a is slow, the request for q=ab is fast; q=a resolves last and replaces the 'ab' results, so the table shows results for a different query than the box. Requests also number one per keystroke.
remediation: Debounce input by about 250 ms, abort the previous request with AbortController, and ignore a response whose request id is not the latest.

title: Refund is sent on first click with no confirmation, though the README says refunds are confirmed
evidence: app.js:49-51 goes straight from click to refund(); no confirm(), dialog or summary exists in app.js or index.html. README.md:9 states 'Refunds are confirmed before they are sent.'
failing_case: One misclick on 'Refund selected' sends a money-moving POST with whatever ids are in `selected`. There is no undo.
remediation: Show a confirm step that lists the count and total to be refunded with Cancel and 'Refund 3 orders' buttons; send only on confirm. Correct or delete the README line until it is true.

title: Several text colours fail 4.5:1: card labels, pager buttons, eyebrow, Refund button
evidence: Computed with the WCAG formula: #aaa on #fff (.lbl) = 2.3:1 at 11px; #aaa on #F4F1EA (button, styles.css:18, 12px) = about 2.1:1; #c7c2f0 on #6366f1 (.eyebrow, styles.css:4, 11px) = about 2.6:1; #fff on #8b5cf6 (.refund, styles.css:12) = about 4.2:1. WCAG 1.4.3 (AA).
failing_case: A low-vision user cannot read 'REVENUE', 'ORDERS', 'Prev', 'Next' or the page indicator context; 11-12 px text makes it worse.
remediation: Use at least #595959 on white and on the cream background for small text, raise sizes to 14 px or more, and darken the Refund background to meet 4.5:1 with white text.

title: Table is fixed at 1000 px, so the page scrolls sideways at 390 px; the 3-column cards and the 120 px clipped name column do not adapt either
evidence: Driven at 390x800: document scrollWidth 1024 vs clientWidth 390. styles.css:6 keeps three columns of cards; styles.css:15 clips the customer name at 120 px with overflow:hidden and no ellipsis or title.
failing_case: On a phone the operator must scroll sideways to reach the Status column; long customer names are cut mid-word with no way to read them.
remediation: Use width:100% with a horizontally scrollable wrapper or a stacked card layout under 600 px; switch .cards to one column under 600 px; add text-overflow:ellipsis and a title.

title: Order status is shown only as a coloured dot with no text or accessible name
evidence: app.js:32 renders , an empty element. Green vs red vs yellow is the sole signal; WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Colour (A) and 1.1.1.
failing_case: A colour-blind user, or any screen-reader user, cannot tell paid from refunded orders, which is the information needed before refunding.
remediation: Render the status word in the cell (optionally with the dot), or add visually-hidden text; use a shape or label, not hue alone.

title: Focus outline removed from buttons, inputs and selects with no replacement
evidence: styles.css:19 sets outline:none on all three; nothing in styles.css defines :focus-visible. WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA).
failing_case: Tab through the toolbar and pager: no control shows where focus is.
remediation: Delete the rule, or replace it with :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1a1a1a; outline-offset: 2px } with at least 3:1 contrast.

title: Refund can be submitted twice: no in-flight guard, no idempotency key, and the selection is not cleared
evidence: The handler has no disabled/busy state, calls refund() with the live `selected` array, and never empties it. api.js:11 sends no Idempotency-Key header.
failing_case: Operator double-clicks Refund selected (or clicks again because the toast lingers). Two identical POST /refunds requests with the same ids go out; the backend may refund twice.
remediation: Disable the control while a refund is in flight, send a per-action idempotency key, and clear the selection only after a confirmed result.

title: Search text is put into the URL without encoding
evidence: Driven: typing `a&status=paid#x` sent GET /orders?q=a&status=paid; the typed '&status=paid' became a parameter and '#x' was dropped as a fragment.
failing_case: Search for a customer named 'Smith & Sons': the server receives q=Smith and an empty parameter ' Sons', so results are wrong; a typed '&status=refunded' overrides the dropdown filter.
remediation: Build the query with URLSearchParams or encodeURIComponent for each value.

title: Discount, tax rate and revenue rule are hard-coded inside the render function
evidence: app.js:12-16 applies a 10% gold discount and an 8.25% tax multiplier inside renderStats(). The table shows o.total raw (app.js:32), so the stats and the table use different numbers for the same orders. Tax is added to revenue, and refunded orders are subtracted although the status is the order's current state, so a refunded order with no matching paid row gives negative revenue (driven: REVENUE $-105.33).
failing_case: A gold customer's order of $100 shows $100 in the table but contributes $97.43 to REVENUE (100*0.9*1.0825). Change the tax rate and the number must be edited inside a view function.
remediation: Extract a pure, tested function (orderNet, summarize) with named constants, or use totals the server computes; the view only formats the result.

title: AVG ORDER divides by zero on an empty result and shows $NaN
evidence: Driven: a search with no matches gives 'REVENUE $0.00 / ORDERS 0 / $NaN AVG ORDER'. The average also divides net revenue by all orders, including refunded and pending ones.
failing_case: Type a name that matches nothing, or filter to a status with no rows: the third card reads '$NaN'.
remediation: Guard orders.length === 0 and show an em dash or empty state; define the average over paid orders in the pure stats function.

title: Prev and Next are unbounded and never reset on search or filter
evidence: Driven: after 4 Next clicks the label read 'Page 5 of 2' and the table was empty; after 6 Prev clicks, 'Page -1 of 2'. load() (app.js:38-43) keeps the old `page` after a new search.
failing_case: User on page 3 types a query that returns 4 results: table is empty, no message, because page is still 3.
remediation: Clamp page to [1, pageCount], disable Prev/Next at the ends, set page = 1 in load().

title: No loading, empty or error state: a blank table and 'Page 1 of 0' with no explanation
evidence: tbody is empty at first paint and for any zero-result query; no message element exists in index.html or app.js. Driven: empty result gave an empty table, 'Page 1 of 0', and $NaN.
failing_case: First load on a slow network shows an empty grid; a search with no match shows the same grid. The user cannot tell loading from no results from failure.
remediation: Add a status row/region: 'Loading orders...', 'No orders match "x". Clear the search.', and 'Could not load orders (HTTP 500). Retry'.

title: The result toast is not a live region, so the refund outcome is never announced
evidence: index.html:23 has no role=status or aria-live. app.js:51 sets textContent and display:block only; nothing ever hides it again.
failing_case: A screen-reader user clicks Refund: no announcement. The toast also stays on screen until reload and its text is stale on the next refund.
remediation: Add role="status" aria-live="polite" to the container (present at load), and auto-hide or give it a dismiss button.

title: Toast pulses forever with no prefers-reduced-motion override
evidence: styles.css:20-21 loops a scale animation indefinitely; no @media (prefers-reduced-motion) exists in styles.css. WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A) for moving content over 5 seconds.
failing_case: A user with vestibular sensitivity who has reduced motion enabled still sees the toast pulse until reload.
remediation: Remove the animation, or run it once and wrap it in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference).

title: Search box and status select have no label; placeholder is the only name; row checkboxes and the first column header are unnamed
evidence: index.html:17-18 have no <label>, aria-label or aria-labelledby; index.html:21 has an empty <th>; each row checkbox (app.js:32) has no name. WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2 (A).
failing_case: A screen reader announces 'edit text' and 'combo box' with no purpose, and 'checkbox' ten times with no indication of which order each selects, so the user cannot choose what to refund.
remediation: Add visible or visually-hidden labels for #q and #status; give each checkbox aria-label="Select order <id> for <customer>"; give the first th a hidden 'Select' text.

title: Refund with nothing selected still sends a request and announces 'Refunded 0 orders!'; the message is also ungrammatical for 1 order
evidence: Driven: with selected = [] the click still POSTed /refunds and the toast read 'Refunded 0 orders!'. Single selection gives '1 orders'. The message claims completion before anything is verified.
failing_case: Click Refund selected with no boxes checked: the operator is told 'Refunded 0 orders!' and an empty POST has been made.
remediation: Disable the button until at least one order is selected, return early on an empty list, pluralise, and word the message from the server's confirmed result ('3 orders refunded').
